brief: SpaceX's public float has risen from 5% at IPO to roughly a third of shares as investor lockups expire, and Goldman expects about half to be free-floating by mid-2027. Rising float is lifting SpaceX's weight across equity indices and passive ownership: ETFs held roughly $30bn of SpaceX (1.5% of its market cap) at end-October, about $20bn of it Nasdaq-100-benchmarked, and a December 11 Russell 1000 Growth rebalance could add over $10bn more demand. The Nasdaq-100's own methodology, a 3x float-market-cap multiplier below 33% float and full market cap above it, mutes the mechanical weight increase as float keeps rising. SpaceX is not yet an S&P 500 constituent; GS expects its GAAP-profitability eligibility condition to be met once Q2 2027 results print, alongside the 12-month seasoning requirement, pointing to possible H2 2027 inclusion, with a merger into an existing constituent a separate possible path. Despite being the largest US IPO on record, SpaceX's effect on Nasdaq-100 valuation, return, and volatility has been small, a pattern GS likens to Tesla's 2020 S&P 500 inclusion. As of June 30, insiders and stakeholders still held about 70% of shares, versus roughly 5% for hedge funds, mutual funds, and ETFs combined.
